name: pwm_controller
description: Parameterized PWM controller with synchronous enable-controlled counter, programmable period wrap, programmable duty comparison, and synchronous active-low reset. The controller emits a PWM waveform and the current counter value on the rising edge of clk.

fixed_assumptions: duty_cycle and period are sampled combinationally for PWM comparison and wrap decision in the same clocked domain.
If enable is low, counter_value holds its previous registered value.
If period is 0, the counter wraps to 0 on the first enabled clock edge so the counter remains bounded.
If duty_cycle is 0, pwm_out is low for all counter values.
If duty_cycle exceeds period, pwm_out may remain high whenever counter_value is below duty_cycle, subject to the current counter value.

feature_contracts.description: Synchronous active-low reset clears observable outputs and internal registered count to zero.
With reset released and enable asserted, the registered counter increments on each clock until wrap conditions apply.
When enable is low, the registered counter holds its value across clock edges.
When the counter reaches the programmed period value and enable remains high, the next enabled clock edge forces the counter back to zero.
PWM output is high whenever the registered counter value is less than the duty cycle.
PWM output is low when the registered counter value is greater than or equal to the duty cycle.

functionality: Implements a synchronous 8-bit PWM generator. The internal counter increments by one on each rising edge of clk when enable is asserted. When the counter reaches the programmed period value, the next enabled increment causes the counter to reset to zero rather than continuing past the period. The PWM output is a combinational function of the registered counter value and the current duty_cycle setting: pwm_out is asserted when counter_value is less than duty_cycle and deasserted otherwise. The design supports synchronous reset of all registers to zero when reset_n is low.
responsibilities: Generate a wrap-bounded modulo-like count sequence controlled by period.
Generate a PWM output from the registered count and duty threshold.
Provide a stable counter_value output for observation and integration.
Honor synchronous active-low reset behavior for all registers.
reset_behavior: On a rising edge of clk while reset_n is low, counter_value is synchronously cleared to 8'h00 and any output registers are cleared to 1'b0. After reset deassertion, the counter resumes from zero on the next enabled clock edge.
behavior_rules: On every rising edge of clk, if reset_n is low, all sequential state is cleared to zero.
On every rising edge of clk, if reset_n is high and enable is low, counter_value retains its previous value.
On every rising edge of clk, if reset_n is high and enable is high, counter_value increments by 1 unless it has reached period, in which case it resets to 0.
The comparison for pwm_out is level-based: pwm_out is 1 when counter_value < duty_cycle, else 0.
counter_value is an output reflection of the registered counter state, not a separate independently computed count.
The design must remain synthesizable using only registers, comparators, and simple control logic.
The design must not infer latches.
All arithmetic is unsigned and 8-bit wide.
The controller does not contain memory macros or hierarchical submodules.
